newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr falls sharply versus yen on strong BOJ tankan.
newsitem.headline: Dlr falls sharply versus yen on strong BOJ tankan.

text.p: ASIAN FOREX ACTIVITY:
*Dollar fell nearly one yen from late New York level in early Tokyo after stronger-than-expected Bank of Japan tankan.
*Stop-loss dollar sales triggered around 114 yen, taking dollar down to 113.80, dealers said.
*Key diffusion index for major manufacturers in June tankan was plus seven, up from plus two in March and above a range of forecasts given by economists of from minus four to plus four.
*Interbank players rushed to set up new dollar shorts after tankan, traders said.

*"Judging from the tankan, there may be a chance that the Bank of Japan will raise interest rates in the autumn. In addition to liquidation of longs, players have set up new dollar shorts after the tankan's release," said a city bank trader.
*Dollar pared part of its losses on short-covering after falling to 113.80 yen, a trust bank trader said.
*Dollar could slide further to around 113.50 yen, but buying interest from Japanese institutional investors likely to provide support at around 113 yen, a trader at another trust bank said.
*Traders took note of the fact that the diffusion index (DI) for major manufacturers is forecast to rise to plus eight in September.
*"The DI forecast for September is very strong, which could provide an argument in favour of credit tightening," said trader at a city bank.
*Others, however, said it may be too early to come to any conclusions about the timing of a BOJ credit tightening.
*"The DI for small manufacturers remained weak and is forecast to drop in September. So it may be too early to say the BOJ will tighten in the autumn," a trust bank trader said.
*DI for small manufacturers improved just slightly in June to minus seven from minus eight in March, but is forecast to fall to minus eight again in September.
*"We will be watching Japanese government bond and euroyen futures for clues about Japanese interest rates," said trader at a trust bank.
*Key September JGB futures dropped sharply after tankan, falling as low as 123.21 from Tuesday's close of 124.41.
*Yen also gained sharply against European currencies in cross trade. Mark/yen stood at 66.09/12 yen at 0045 GMT, down from around 66.64 yen in late New York on Tuesday.
*Dollar ended higher on Tuesday in New York after Japanese officials downplayed fears that Japan would pare its massive holdings of U.S. government securities.
*Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters on Tuesday that Japan had not sold U.S. Treasuries and had no intention of doing so.

*Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto triggered a sharp fall in dollar, U.S. stocks and bonds on Monday by saying that Japan had in the past been tempted to sell its holdings of U.S. Treasury securities and boost its gold reserves.
-- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
